title: Pakistan Supreme Court Orders Jailed Ex-PM Imran Khan Moved to Hospital
excerpt: The 73-year-old former cricket star, imprisoned since 2023, will be transferred to Shifa International Hospital within 48 hours after suffering severe vision loss in custody.
body:
• Pakistan's Supreme Court ordered former PM Imran Khan transferred from jail to Shifa International Hospital within 48 hours
  • Khan, 73, has lost 85% of vision in his right eye due to central retinal vein occlusion that went untreated for months in custody
  • The court directed he remain hospitalized until September 16, meeting longstanding demands from his party and family
  • Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 on charges he says are politically motivated following his 2022 ouster

Pakistan's Supreme Court on Tuesday ordered that former Prime Minister Imran Khan be moved from prison to a hospital, his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party confirmed, ending months of legal wrangling over the jailed leader's deteriorating health.

The court directed that Khan, 73, be transferred to Islamabad's Shifa International Hospital within 48 hours and remain there until September 16, according to PTI spokesperson Naeem Haider Panjutha, who posted the details on X.

A Long Battle Over Medical Care

The ruling addresses a crisis that has shadowed Khan's imprisonment for over a year. The cricketer-turned-politician has been in jail since August 2023, convicted in a series of cases involving state gifts, an alleged unlawful marriage, and corruption — all of which he denies, calling them politically driven.

https://x.com/republicpolicy/status/2089638532390514902

Khan's health became a flashpoint in February when his lawyer, Salman Safdar, told the Supreme Court that the former premier had lost 85% of the vision in his right eye. Doctors attributed the damage to central retinal vein occlusion, a condition that his legal team said had gone effectively untreated since Khan first reported worsening eyesight in October 2025.

"It's a very welcome order and we wish it had happened sooner so his eye and general health would not have deteriorated this much."

— Zulfikar Bukhari, PTI Spokesperson

According to court filings reviewed by Reuters, Khan was given only eye drops for more than three months despite repeated complaints. Requests to allow his personal physicians to examine him were denied, and routine blood tests were not conducted. A brief eye procedure at a government hospital in January provided only limited relief.

Political Stakes and International Pressure

Khan was removed from power through a parliamentary no-confidence vote in April 2022. Since then, he has faced dozens of criminal cases in what his supporters describe as a military-backed campaign to sideline Pakistan's most popular opposition leader.

PTI, which won power in the 2018 general election, was stripped of its election symbol ahead of the February 2024 vote, forcing its candidates to run as independents. Despite these restrictions, PTI-backed candidates emerged as the single largest bloc, though other parties formed a coalition government under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

The case has drawn significant international attention. In February, cricket greats from around the world — including players from India — issued a public statement expressing "deep concern" about Khan's prison conditions and demanding better medical treatment for the former Pakistan cricket captain.

What Comes Next

The hospital transfer marks the most significant concession by Pakistani authorities since Khan's imprisonment began three years ago. Legal observers say the order reflects mounting judicial discomfort with the handling of Khan's medical care, particularly after the attorney general acknowledged before the court that the government bears a duty to provide adequate healthcare to inmates.

"He should remain in hospital until all doctors are satisfied," Bukhari told Reuters.

Khan's sons, Kasim and Sulaiman, who are based in London, have separately sought visas to visit their father in Pakistan. The two, aged 26 and 29, told Reuters in February that they had spoken to their father for the first time since September during a phone call in which he expressed frustration over being denied timely treatment.

Some of Khan's convictions have been suspended or overturned on appeal, while others remain pending. His political future — and whether he will eventually be released — remains the most charged question in Pakistani politics.
